topic: RAII Tying Resources to Object Lifetimes
explanation: RAII is a fundamental C++ idiom that ties the lifetime of a resource to the lifetime of an object. In practical terms, resources (like file handles, network connections, or mutexes) are acquired in a object's constructor and released in its destructor. This ensures that resources are automatically and reliably cleaned up when the object goes out of scope, even if an exception occurs. In real-world scenarios, such as managing database connections or file I/O, RAII prevents resource leaks, reduces error-prone manual cleanup, and promotes exception-safe code. Best practices include using standard library tools like std::unique_ptr or std::lock_guard for automatic management, avoiding raw pointers, and always preferring RAII over explicit release calls to minimize bugs.
